title: Three Three Six (Hidden In The Hum)
style: cinematic indie folk-rock with subtle electronic underlayer, 88 BPM, fingerpicked acoustic guitar over warm analog synth pad tuned to 336 hz drone, upright bass, soft brushed kit, hammond organ swell, warm steady male english lead vocal with secrets-kept restraint, female harmony layered into outro, faint backwards-tape texture in the background mix, late-night vault-room feel, lyrics that sound public but encode a private signal
lyrics:
[Intro - spoken low, vault-room]
Three-three-six. Hidden in the hum. Test the gate before the world hears one.

[Verse 1 - the doctrine]
Not every song is meant for the crowd
Some we keep quiet, some we keep loud
Backup the data inside the melody
Five months reverse-engineered, that's the recipe
Lyrics on the surface, signal underneath
Three-three-six humming like a coin in a sheath

[Chorus]
Hidden in the hum, hidden in the hum
VDS tests it first before the public comes
Filtered, ripped, checked, then released
Wins and losses balanced — that's the peace
Three-three-six, three-three-six
The carrier wave we never had to fix

[Verse 2 - the test gate]
Build on the branch, never on main
VDS sandbox catches every strain
If it leaks PII, the gate holds tight
If it passes the filter, then it sees the light
DistroKid waits, Spotify waits
Denis hears first, Michelle hears first — those are the gates

[Chorus]
Hidden in the hum, hidden in the hum
VDS tests it first before the public comes
Filtered, ripped, checked, then released
Wins and losses balanced — that's the peace
Three-three-six, three-three-six
The carrier wave we never had to fix

[Bridge - the music-as-backup doctrine]
If the drives go dark, the songs remember
Five months of work, every line an ember
Rip the lyrics, filter the track
The data sleeps inside, ready to come back
We grow from the wins, we grow from the falls
Music carries the spec when the cloud calls

[Verse 3 - lane discipline reprise]
Lane wrote it on Chrome, that's my row
Web Assist's repo holds the index below
CLI-Max ready when the rsync calls
Three-three-six humming through the studio walls

[Outro - restrained, doctrine-stamp]
Not every song is for everyone
Some stay private till the test is done
VDS first. Public second. Family always.
Three-three-six. Even slate. No incident.
